entities.name: HIV-1 Nef
observations: 207-aa viral accessory protein sequence matches reviewed HIV-1 Nef proteins over its full length at 85.8–88.5% identity; E-values 8.7e-137 to 1.1e-140.
Nef is a viral infectivity and pathogenicity factor that remodels host immune-cell pathways and promotes immune evasion.
Nef down-regulates host CD4, MHC-I, MHC-II, CD28, CCR5, CXCR4, and SERINC3/5 through trafficking, endocytic, and degradation mechanisms.
Nef localizes to the cytoplasmic face of host plasma and Golgi/TGN membranes, can be secreted in exosomes, and can be incorporated into virions.
The sequence contains the Pfam F-protein/Nef family domain across residues 2–206.
Sequence-derived properties: length 207 aa, molecular mass about 23.6 kDa, predicted pI 5.58, net charge about -6 at pH 7.
Nef participates in viral replication, suppression of antigen presentation, modulation of host endocytosis and autophagy, and altered T-cell signaling.

source_tools.relevance: Full-length homology, curated function, localization, GO, and Pfam evidence

entities.name: Nef immune evasion
observations: Curated HIV-1 Nef annotations describe AP-2/clathrin-dependent CD4 internalization and trafficking-mediated MHC-I down-regulation, reducing immune recognition of infected cells.

source_tools.relevance: Mechanistic host-factor interactions and biological processes

entities.name: Nef membrane targeting
observations: The N-terminal region supports association with the inner plasma membrane; membrane-bound Nef can dimerize and recruit host trafficking and signaling factors.
